hints: Notice the wave travels through a vacuum, so its speed must be $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and must satisfy $c = \lambda / T$.

Convert each prefixed unit to base SI units before dividing: $1 \text{ Tm} = 10^{12} \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ pm} = 10^{-12} \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ } \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ Ms} = 10^6 \text{ s}$, $1 \text{ Gs} = 10^9 \text{ s}$ and $1 \text{ ns} = 10^{-9} \text{ s$.
Calculate $\lambda / T$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for each row and keep only the pair whose ratio is $3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: All electromagnetic waves in vacuum travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the correct pair must satisfy $v = \lambda / T = c$.
Convert the wavelength and period to metres and seconds. For the successful pair, $\lambda = 1.2 \times 10^2 \text{ pm} = 1.2 \times 10^2 \times 10^{-12} \text{ m} = 1.2 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
Convert its period: $T = 4.0 \times 10^{-10} \text{ ns} = 4.0 \times 10^{-10} \times 10^{-9} \text{ s} = 4.0 \times 10^{-19} \text{ s}$.
Divide to check the speed: $v = \lambda / T = (1.2 \times 10^{-10}) / (4.0 \times 10^{-19}) = 0.30 \times 10^9 = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
This matches $c$ with correct units of $\text{m s}^{-1}$, while the other pairs give values such as $10^{-5}$, $10^{-32}$ or $10^5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option C.
